title: Frontend Testing and Accessibility knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which test strategy provides stronger evidence than a single passing happy-path example?
options: Only measure line coverage and assume that proves correctness.
Mock every component so no integration is ever checked.
Test expected behavior, edge cases and failure paths, and add type-level tests for public type contracts where useful.
questions.answer_key: Test expected behavior, edge cases and failure paths, and add type-level tests for public type contracts where useful.
questions.explanation: Coverage is a signal, not proof; test quality depends on assertions, cases and realistic boundaries.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about “Frontend Testing and Accessibility”?
options: A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.
The concept should be demonstrated with component testing and checked against its intended contract.
The safest approach is to skip diagnostics and trust the first output.
questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with component testing and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “Component testing”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “Frontend Testing and Accessibility”?
options: Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
Check semantic html and accessible events, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
Assume typed test utilities is unnecessary because the code has type annotations.
Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
questions.answer_key: Check semantic html and accessible events, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.explanation: The syllabus includes “Semantic HTML and accessible events”. Verification should match the concept: type-level checks, runtime tests, configuration checks or human review as appropriate.
